# AI-Trader: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents in Real-Time Financial Markets

arXiv [2512.10971](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10971) · v1 2025-12-01 · latest 2025-12-01

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | A live, fully autonomous, data-uncontaminated benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' financial trading decisions across U.S. stocks, A-shares and cryptocurrencies. | “we introduce AI-Trader, the first fully-automated, live, and data-uncontaminated evaluation benchmark for LLM agents in financial decision-making.” |
| **architecture** | Decoupled live trading environment and ReAct-style trading agents with minimal context (prices, holdings, tools), using MCP tools: Check Price, Search, News, Math, Trade; Buy/Sell/Hold actions with rejection and self-correction on liquidity violations. | “The AI-Trader framework consists of two fully decoupled components: the Live Trading Environment (Sec.3.1) and the Trading Agents (Sec. 3.2).” |
| **data** | Nasdaq-100 constituents plus cash (hourly), SSE-50 constituents (daily), and 10 USDT crypto pairs tracked by the Bitwise Index (daily); prices, web search and financial news via tools. | “We employ a daily-frequency strategy for trading A-shares and cryptocurrencies, while monitoring and recording U.S. equity trades using an hourly-frequency strategy.” |
| **window** | Live trading: U.S. equities and A-shares October 1, 2025 to November 7, 2025; cryptocurrency November 1 to November 14, 2025. No training split (benchmark of pretrained LLMs). | “we present live trading results for U.S. equities and A-shares from October 1, 2025, to November 7, 2025, along with a detailed evaluation and analysis of the cryptocurrency market from November 1 to November 14, 2025.” |
| **models** | DeepSeek-v3.1, MiniMax-M2, Claude-3.7-sonnet, GPT-5, Qwen3-max, Gemini-2.5-flash, each wrapped in identical agents. | “The AI-Trader employs six mainstream models as baselines: DeepSeek-v3.1 (Liu et al., 2024), MiniMax-M2 (MiniMax, 2025), Claude-3.7-sonnet (Anthropic, 2025a) , GPT-5 (OpenAI, 2025), Qwen3-max (Yang et al., 2025), and Gemini-2.5-flash (Comanici et al., 2025).” |
| **baselines** | Market benchmarks: QQQ Invesco (U.S.), SSE-50 index (A-shares), CD5 Index (crypto); LLMs compared against each other. | “AI trading strategies more easily generate excess returns in highly liquid markets. In the U.S. market, multiple AI agents achieved positive excess returns: MiniMax-M2 (+7.69% excess), DeepSeek-v3.1 (+6.52% excess), and even Claude-3.7-Sonnet (+1.24% excess) all outperformed QQQ.” |
| **headline_result** | U.S. market (Oct 1–Nov 7, 2025, hourly): MiniMax-M2 cumulative return 9.56% vs QQQ 1.87%, Sortino 4.42, MDD -4.92%; no agent beat SSE-50 (1.65%); in crypto only DeepSeek-v3.1 beat CD5 (-12.18% vs -14.30%). | “In the U.S. market, MiniMax-M2 achieves a cumulative return of 9.56% (significantly higher than QQQ’s 1.87%) and the highest Sortino ratio among all models at 4.42, while limiting maximum drawdown to -4.92%, outperforming all AI models except the benchmark.” |

| **limitations** | Agents lack a systematic information verification module and can be swayed by single news sources; poor returns, weak risk management and poor cross-market generalization of current agents. | “the decision-making mechanism lacks a systematic information verification module, making it prone to forming judgments based on a single information source, which can easily lead to misjudgments in highly volatile and information-dense market conditions.” |
